chief_complaint: fever, cough with yellow sputum, and focal lung crackles
hpi_details: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with fever, cough with yellow sputum, and focal lung crackles. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks a nasty head cold she caught from her coworker traveled into her chest and turned into severe acute bronchitis.
concerns: She is worried that she will be admitted to the hospital, leaving nobody to care for her two young children as a single mother.
expectations: She hopes to receive a chest X-ray and a prescription for oral antibiotics so she can recover safely at home.

investigation_events.title: Urgent pneumonia results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent chest radiograph and blood count are now available.

results.value: Focal right lower-lobe air-space consolidation with air bronchograms; no pleural effusion

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Community-Acquired Pneumonia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Oral Amoxicillin 1g TID or Doxycycline for 5 days, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: fever, cough with yellow sputum, and focal lung crackles

Key HPI features: A 38-year-old female presents to the clinic with fever, cough with yellow sputum, and focal lung crackles. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 38.5C, HR 102, RR 20, BP 122/78, SpO2 95% on room air. Focal inspiratory crackles and dullness to percussion over the right lower lung field. Chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. WBC 14,200/uL with left shift.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Community-Acquired Pneumonia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bronchitis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Severe breathlessness or confusion.
management_principles: Plan for Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Oral Amoxicillin 1g TID or Doxycycline for 5 days
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 38.5C, HR 102, RR 20, BP 122/78, SpO2 95% on room air. Focal inspiratory crackles and dullness to percussion over the right lower lung field. Chest X-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. WBC 14,200/uL with left shift.
reference_soap.assessment: Community-Acquired Pneumonia, right lower lobe; low-risk by CURB-65, appropriate for outpatient management.

teaching.one_liner: A bacterial lung infection causing fever, productive cough with colored sputum, and focal crackles on exam.

must_ask.say: What color is the sputum you're coughing up?
How long have you had this cough?
Any chest pain, especially with breathing?

history.answer: I have had a high fever and a bad cough with thick yellow phlegm for the past three days, and I feel completely exhausted.
The fever started about three days ago and has been gradually getting worse each day.
The highest reading was 38.5 degrees Celsius on my digital thermometer yesterday. The fever is constant throughout the day and comes with severe shaking chills.
I took acetaminophen yesterday evening. It brought the fever down slightly for a couple of hours, but then it spiked right back up.
I've been coughing frequently and bringing up thick, yellowish-green mucus, especially in the mornings.
I feel slightly out of breath when I walk across the room or cough repeatedly, but I am not gasping for air when resting.
I feel a sharp, catching pain on the lower right side of my chest whenever I take a deep breath or cough hard.
No, I don't have a sore throat, runny nose, or stuffy nose.
No burning when I urinate, no frequent urination, and no flank or back pain.
No nausea, vomiting, stomach cramps, or diarrhea.
I have a mild, generalized headache from the fever, but my neck is not stiff and my thoughts are completely clear.
No skin rashes, insect bites, black scabs, or joint swelling and pain.
I sweat a lot when the fever temporarily dips, but I haven't had chronic drenching night sweats or any weight loss.
No, I haven't noticed any lumps or swelling in my neck, armpits, or groin.
I haven't traveled outside the country recently, haven't gone hiking or done farm work, and don't have contact with animals.
No one at my home or in my office has been sick with a cough or fever recently.
No, I have never had cancer, never received chemotherapy, and don't take steroids or immunosuppressants.
No heart conditions, artificial heart valves, or recent dental cleanings or procedures.
No, I haven't started any new prescription medications recently.
I am married and only sexually active with my husband, and I have never used intravenous or recreational drugs.
I have always been healthy with no history of asthma, diabetes, hypertension, or other chronic illnesses.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I don't take any regular prescription medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements, just the over-the-counter acetaminophen yesterday.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or seasonal allergens.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or vaping products.
I only have an occasional glass of wine at social dinners, maybe once or twice a month.
I work in an office as an accountant and live with my husband in an apartment.
Both my parents and my older brother are alive and healthy with no history of chronic lung disease.
My last period started two weeks ago, my cycles are regular every 28 days, we use barrier contraception, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

I thought maybe that bad cold going around my office just settled in my chest and turned into severe bronchitis. I'm really worried that I'll have to be admitted to the hospital when there's nobody else at home to look after my two young kids.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 122/78 mmHg, heart rate 102 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, temperature 38.5°C, oxygen saturation 95% on room air.
Pharyngeal mucosa is normal and pink without erythema, exudate, or tonsillar swelling.
Bilateral tympanic membranes are intact, translucent, and pearly gray without erythema or effusion.
No palpable cervical, submental, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Dullness to percussion over the right lower lung field; resonant over all other lung zones.
Focal inspiratory crackles over the right lower lung base; clear breath sounds bilaterally in upper and mid lung fields.
Tachycardia with regular rhythm; normal S1 and S2 with no murmurs, rubs, or gallops heard.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender without guarding, rebound tenderness, or organomegaly.
Warm and dry skin with no petechiae, rashes, purpura, or eschar.
Supple neck with full passive flexion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
